biography: Greg Crick burst onto the Australian racing scene almost overnight. Hailing from a small sheep farming town in New South Wales, his first taste of speed came not on asphalt, but on dusty outback tracks, modifying his father's old ute for informal races with friends. It wasn't until he turned 18 that he even saw a proper racetrack. He attended a local V8 Supercar race and was instantly hooked. He scraped together every penny he could, sold his prized motorcycle, and enrolled in a racing school. His raw talent was immediately apparent. Within a year, he'd won a state-level championship, attracting the attention of Adrenaline Red, a team known for taking chances on young, unproven drivers. Now at 21, Crick is considered one of Australia's most promising rising stars, with several podium finishes already under his belt. His aggressive driving style and relentless determination are quickly making him a fan favorite, though they've also earned him a few enemies on the track.
drivingStyle: Crick's driving style is characterized by its raw aggression and fearless corner entries. He's known for late braking and isn't afraid to push the car right to its limit – and sometimes beyond. Tire management isn't exactly his strong suit; he tends to burn through rubber quickly in his relentless pursuit of every tenth of a second. Under pressure, Crick can be both brilliant and erratic. While he thrives in wheel-to-wheel combat, he's also prone to making costly mistakes when the stakes are high, a trait the team are working hard on

famousQuote: "I'm not here to make friends; I'm here to win races. If that ruffles a few feathers along the way, so be it."
careerHighlight: Winning the Sandown 500 in his rookie year after starting from the back of the grid due to a mechanical issue in qualifying. He carved his way through the field with a series of daring overtakes.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the Gold Coast 600 due to overdriving the car, costing his team a guaranteed victory and severely damaging his reputation.
